comparator.sourceNotes: The selected standard Spanish pathway closes 60+60+60 with a 127.5-EC major and 52.5 EC of genuine profiling. The odd 2027-2028 package uses the formal prospective title Testimonios, crónicas, representaciones. Research Methods Intercultural Communication remains an eligible neutral selection, although Methods and Statistics 1 is now listed first. Writing preparation and the Spanish thesis remain separate. The 30-EC approved coherent profile and remaining 22.5 EC stay generic. Mandatory grammar test MT1V11002 is zero-credit and is not added to the total. Formal and selected-course evidence support Spanish, English and Dutch instruction.

routeSelection.basis: The generic normalized target does not name the optional Crossing Borders track. The standard Trans-Atlantic Perspectives package most directly represents the programme's Spanish-language, Spanish and Latin American identity. The odd-year package applies when a Fall-2026 entrant reaches Year 2; two first-listed even-year courses complete the required six-course depth sequence in Year 3. The first-listed methods option breaks the remaining neutral tie. All selections were fixed before UCR fit was considered.

alternatives.label: Colonial histories, global literature & cultural memory
alternatives.concept: Study literature, empire, colonial and postcolonial histories, migration, cultural memory, heritage, media and language/power across transatlantic and global contexts. Treat these as related humanities and social-science approaches while preserving the absence of Spanish-language proficiency and a sustained Spain/Latin America sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The label names the completed curriculum’s literature, empire, migration, media, heritage and cultural-memory content without claiming Spanish-language study or a full Spain/Latin America curriculum.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and ten level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; the only formal prerequisite, Introduction to Brain & Behavior for Psycholinguistics, occurs two semesters earlier. Introductory literary, historical, sociological and film study precedes advanced interpretation, media, heritage and research. No Spanish-language prerequisite or proficiency is invented.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & language in cultural expression
alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical, linguistic and media forms create meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, film and multimodal cultural production. Preserve Spanish proficiency and Spanish-specific linguistics as explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film and media; it is labelled as cultural-expression study and not as Spanish proficiency or Spanish linguistics.
progression: The schedule has 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in year one and eight level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. Introductory literature, rhetoric, sociology and film/media precede advanced stylistic, persuasive, creative, interpretive and documentary work. No French-language competence is implied by this progression.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Native American Histories, European Union Politics and three art/heritage courses are replaced by Rhetorical Communication, Rhetoric in Action, Persuasive Communication, Creative Communication Laboratory and From T.V. to TikTok. The change shifts advanced study from colonial histories, heritage and cultural memory to language, rhetoric and mediated expression.

candidates.label: Language, identity, intercultural communication and contemporary cultural expression

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. A third Spanish-language proficiency and linguistics programme is not feasible because the workbook contains no Spanish acquisition sequence, advanced Spanish grammar, morphology and syntax, sociolinguistics, translation or Spanish-language writing. Psycholinguistics and stylistics contribute genuine language study but cannot be expanded into or labelled as Spanish proficiency.

blocks: Both examine relations between language, cognition and cultural meaning; UCR is general psycholinguistics rather than Spanish sociolinguistics or Spanish-language study.
Both analyse how linguistic form creates meaning; UCR uses stylistics and literary linguistics rather than comparative Spanish morphology and syntax.
Both develop creative and analytical communication; UCR works across poetry, performance, voice and media rather than professional and academic writing in Spanish.
UCR has no Spanish-language acquisition sequence to CEFR A1.
UCR has no Spanish-language acquisition sequence to CEFR A2.
UCR has no Spanish-language acquisition sequence to CEFR B1.
UCR has no Spanish-language acquisition sequence to CEFR B2.
Psycholinguistics and stylistics do not reproduce the sociolinguistics of Spanish in Spain and Latin America.
UCR has no dedicated course on variation and historical change in Spanish.
Literature, textual interpretation, theatre and film
Both establish literary analysis and interpretation; UCR is a general literary-studies course rather than a Spanish-language sequence.
Both use close reading to connect literary works with historical and cultural contexts; UCR spans a broader canon and does not supply Spanish proficiency.
Both analyse testimony, memoir, travel and culturally situated narrative; UCR is cross-cultural rather than focused on Spain and Latin America.
Both study film, performance and intermedial cultural expression; UCR is not Spanish-language theatre and cinema study.
Colonial histories, migration, cultural memory, heritage and media
Both examine contested colonial pasts, cultural memory and resistance; UCR centres Indigenous histories in North America rather than Spain and Latin America.
Both develop methods for interpreting situated cultural meanings; UCR supplies general qualitative methodology rather than the comparator’s intercultural-communication methods course.
Both address migration, diaspora, inclusion and decolonial critique; UCR is cross-regional rather than specific to the Spanish-speaking world.
External thesis, academic core and open profile
The genuine 22.5-EC profiling space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.
The compulsory Spanish Language and Culture thesis remains separate; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only and not scheduled degree credit.
The genuine approved 30-EC coherent profile remains open and is not replaced by invented external modules.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study global literature, colonial and postcolonial histories, migration, cultural memory, heritage, media, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and language/power. UCR does not offer Spanish proficiency progression, Spanish grammar and linguistics, translation, Spanish-language writing, or a cumulative Spain and Latin America literature/culture sequence, so these are related humanities routes rather than Spanish Language and Culture equivalents.
